scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable in this situation with my boyfriend. Let me start by laying out all the details to make sure I understand everything correctly. First, my partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm. That's a pretty long day, and I can imagine it's exhausting. I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. That seems like a good setup for maintaining a relationship without the pressures of living together. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends. He's 12 years old and really excited about it. Initially, I thought about asking my boyfriend to pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom during a casual visit, she strongly expected me to pay and told me it was my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. Even though he's been in my life for three years, she made it clear that I should handle it. So, I ended up paying for it, but to afford it, I had to extend my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends. Given his work schedule, he looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's responsibility." I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in South London, whereas we live in North London, and his dad doesn't drive, but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad could take him, but what would be a one-hour-plus journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my boyfriend. He got really angry and told me that he had to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games, etc., since I wasn't home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quickly. He then suggested that we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. I was like, "Really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world, love!" The little sneak then went over to see my mom and had a heart-to-heart with her, which ended up in her calling me and telling me I'm out of line. So, who is in the wrong here? Am I being unreasonable, or is my boyfriend? Okay, so breaking this down, there are a few key points: 1. **Financial Responsibility:** My mom expects me to pay for my son's football activities, even though my boyfriend has been in my life for three years. I ended up extending my work hours to afford it. 2. **Logistical Support:** I asked my boyfriend to help with picking up and dropping off my son on weekends, given his ability to drive and the proximity to our home. He refused, citing that it's my responsibility and that he wants to use his weekends for his own activities. 3. **Emotional Response:** I snapped at him, which led to an argument where he suggested breaking up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. 4. **Involvement of Family:** My son went to my mom, leading to her calling me and telling me I'm out of line. So, is it reasonable for me to expect my boyfriend to help with these responsibilities, especially considering his ability to provide logistical support? Or is it fair for him to want to use his weekends for himself, especially after working long hours? Also, how does my mom's involvement play into this? She seems to have a clear expectation that I should handle everything, which might be influencing my approach to the situation. Furthermore, my reaction of snapping at him might have escalated the situation. Is it fair for him to suggest breaking up over this, or is he overreacting? I think it's important to consider the balance of responsibilities in a relationship. While I understand that my mom expects me to handle things, in a relationship, both partners usually share responsibilities, especially when it comes to supporting children's activities. On the other hand, my boyfriend has a demanding job and might need his weekends to unwind. It's also reasonable for him to have his own interests and time to relax. The conflict seems to arise from differing expectations about responsibilities and how to balance them with personal time. Perhaps communication is the key here. Both parties need to express their needs and expectations clearly to find a middle ground. In this case, it might be helpful to discuss how responsibilities can be shared without overwhelming either partner. Maybe there's a way to compromise, such as finding alternative solutions for transportation or adjusting schedules to accommodate both our needs. It's also important to reflect on how external influences, like my mom's expectations, might be affecting my approach to the situation. While her input is valuable, it's crucial to establish boundaries and make decisions that work best for my relationship. Lastly, managing emotions during conflicts is essential. Snapping at my boyfriend likely made him feel defensive, leading to the breakup suggestion. It's important to approach such conversations calmly and rationally to avoid escalation. Overall, while I might feel that my expectations are reasonable, it's also important to consider my boyfriend's needs and find a balanced approach that works for both of us.
